verdict.problem: Supabase covers Firebase's main backend job (database, auth, storage, functions, realtime), so the fit should be full rather than partial.

The second sentence claims Fedora is aimed at people wanting an alternative to Windows or macOS, but Fedora's own page does not position it that way; it presents itself as a Linux distribution for desktops, servers, cloud and developers.

ownCloud is a self-hosted file storage, sync and sharing server with official desktop and mobile sync clients, so it covers the main job of Dropbox and Google Drive and should be listed as full, not partial.
The description presents image editing and layout building as current uses, but the project lists photo editing and desktop publishing as planned roadmap items.
Gnumeric is a complete desktop spreadsheet with formulas and charts, so it does the main job of Excel and should be rated full rather than partial.
The description calls Insomnia a desktop and web app, but the project page only describes desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux (plus a CLI).
WordPress core handles blog publishing but has no built-in email newsletter or paid-subscription features, which are Substack's main job, so 'partial' fits better than 'full'.
Strapi is a headless CMS that matches Contentful but has no site builder or frontend like Wix, Strikingly or Webflow, so 'partial' fits better than 'full'.
SigNoz covers the main job of Datadog and New Relic (APM, logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts and infrastructure monitoring), so the fit should be "full", not "partial".
Kubero is a complete self-hosted Heroku-style PaaS (git deploys, pipelines, review apps, add-ons, logs, domains), so it does the main job and should be rated full rather than partial.
Uptrace covers traces, metrics, logs, dashboards and alerting, the core APM/observability job of Datadog and New Relic, so it should be rated full rather than partial.
CryptPad's Document app is a full real-time collaborative word processor built on OnlyOffice, so 'partial' with 'simpler formatting' understates it; 'full' fits better.
LiveKit covers in-app voice/video and SIP calling but has no SMS or phone numbers of its own, so it only partly replaces Twilio.
Kimai is a full-featured time tracker covering the main job of Toggl and Clockify, so the fit should be 'full', not 'partial'.

The repository only holds SDKs, examples, starters and plugins; the visual editor itself is Builder.io's closed hosted service, which needs an account, so this is not an open-source alternative to these apps.
ERPNext is a complete ERP covering accounting, inventory, manufacturing, assets and projects, so its fit should be full rather than partial.
ReactiveSearch is a front-end UI component library for search interfaces, not a database or search engine, so it does not replace Algolia, Elastic Cloud or the other closed services listed.
LibreSign covers DocuSign's main job (sending documents to internal and external signers, signing order, reminders, tracking and validation), so it should be rated a full fit rather than partial.

Posnic is a complete POS (billing, barcode scanning, returns, stock, receipt hardware, restaurant features), so it does the main job of Square POS and Clover and should be listed as "full", not "partial".
Gogs covers GitHub's core job (repository hosting, issues, pull requests, wiki, organizations), so the fit should be "full" rather than "partial".
